title: You didn’t lose your calling because you were busy.
paragraphs: You didn’t lose your calling because you were busy.
You buried it because you were afraid.
Not loud, obvious fear. Not panic. Not trembling hands.
Quiet fear.

The kind that whispers, “What if you fail?”
The kind that tells you to wait… just a little longer.
The kind that disguises itself as wisdom, caution, even humility.
And before you realized it, what God placed in your hands was already in the ground.
Jesus said it plainly in Gospel of Matthew 25:25:
“I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground.”
Read that again.
“I was afraid…”
That’s where it started. Not rebellion. Not hatred. Fear.
And you’ve felt it.

You knew God was calling you to speak, but you stayed silent.
You knew you were supposed to let go of that sin, but you held on.
You knew you were meant to step out, but you stepped back instead.

God saw it.
You knew.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Fear doesn’t just stop action.
It buries obedience.
And buried obedience still gets judged.
The servant in that parable didn’t waste the talent on wild living. He didn’t destroy it. He didn’t even misuse it.
He protected it.
Guarded it.
Hid it.
And that was enough to be called wicked.
That should shake you.
Because you’ve been telling yourself, “At least I’m not doing anything wrong.”
But Heaven isn’t asking if you avoided evil.
He’s asking why you avoided obedience.

There was a moment—you remember it—when conviction hit you hard.
A moment when truth cut through your excuses.
A moment when you knew God was asking for something real.
And you hesitated.
Not because you didn’t believe.
Because you were afraid.

Afraid of rejection.
Afraid of losing control.
Afraid of what people would think.
Afraid of what following Jesus would actually cost you.
So you buried it.
And then you moved on like nothing happened.
But that moment didn’t disappear.
It’s still there.
Waiting.
Because the Master always returns.
Jesus continues in that same passage, and the tone shifts. The kindness gives way to accountability.
“You wicked and lazy servant…” (Matthew 25:26)
That’s not how people expect Jesus to speak.
But it’s how He speaks to buried obedience.
Because fear, when it replaces trust, becomes disobedience.
Let that settle.
Fear is not neutral.

It either drives you to God…
or it drives you to hide from Him.
There’s no middle ground.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
And this is where everything changes.
Because the story doesn’t end with exposure.
It points to a deeper truth you’ve been avoiding.
You don’t just need courage.
You need a Savior.
Because the real issue wasn’t the talent.
It was the heart.
A heart that didn’t trust the Master.
A heart that saw Him as harsh instead of good.
That’s why the servant hid what he was given—he misunderstood who he was serving.
And that’s you, if you’re honest.
You’ve seen God as someone waiting to punish your failure, not a Father who gave His Son to rescue you from it.
But Scripture cuts through that lie.
“For God gave us not a spirit of fear, but of power and love and self-control.” (2 Timothy 1:7)
And even deeper—
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
You weren’t saved because you performed well.
You were saved because Jesus obeyed perfectly where you didn’t.
Where you buried, He surrendered.
Where you hesitated, He obeyed—even to the point of death.
The cross is proof.
Fear doesn’t have the final word.
Grace does.
But grace is not permission to keep burying what God has called you to live out.
Grace is the power to finally step out of the ground.
So now you’re standing in a moment again.
Not the same moment as before.
This one feels heavier.
Clearer.

You can keep hiding.
Keep delaying.
Keep convincing yourself that “later” is enough.
Or you can face the truth:
You were never meant to bury what God entrusted to you.
You were meant to multiply it for His glory.

One path leads to deeper regret.
The other leads to transformation.
And you already know which one you’ve been avoiding.
Say it plainly.
“I’ve been afraid.”
Type it. Admit it. Let it come into the light.
Because the next time fear whispers, you’ll need to remember what it cost you.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—not surface-level inspiration, but real correction, real growth, real discipleship—step into it here:
Because buried faith doesn’t stay buried forever.
One day, it gets uncovered.
